source_text: Dedisti igitur et primi naturam mali, sed inaniorem quam Manichaeus, aeque tamen aeternam. Pugnandum super hoc non est; claret omnino quia maneat inter vos foedus, quod naturalis mali et aeterni mali catena connectit.
pass_a_gloss: You therefore gave also a nature of the first evil, but emptier than Manichaeus, equally nevertheless eternal. One must not fight upon this; it is altogether clear that a treaty remains between you, which a chain of natural evil and of eternal evil connects.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: You have therefore supplied a nature for even the first evil, emptier than Mani’s, but equally eternal. There is no need to fight further about this. It is entirely clear that a pact remains between you, bound by the chain of natural and eternal evil.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
